paper.title: Live-SWE-agent: Can Software Engineering Agents Self-Evolve on the Fly?
paper.central_claim: Live-SWE-agent is the first live software agent that evolves its own scaffold (custom tools) on the fly during runtime, without offline training, reaching 77.4% on SWE-bench Verified and 45.8% on SWE-Bench Pro and beating manually crafted and offline self-improving agents.

signatures.object: Agent action space (tool inventory) of a bash-only mini-SWE-agent; tools are Python scripts written into the task sandbox
signatures.information: Issue text, repository, full trajectory, each command's return code/output (truncated at 10k chars); no hidden test or gold patch visible; the agent writes its own reproduction scripts
signatures.operation: At each step the agent may emit a bash command or write/modify a script (edit, search, file-analyzer, issue-specific tools) and then invoke it by running the script
signatures.output: Script files in the working environment, reused by later commands in the same trajectory
signatures.conditions: Needs a strong LLM able to decide when a tool is useful (weak LLMs loop); cap 250 steps / $3 per issue
signatures.feedback: Execution output of the commands/tools plus the model's own reading of it
signatures.selection_rule: None: the agent alone decides whether to create, keep or abandon a tool; no admission gate, no held-out check, no version/rollback
signatures.persistence: Files in the sandbox for the duration of one issue; discarded after submission (E013)
signatures.later_use: Later steps in the same trajectory call the script; no cross-task reuse tested
signatures.claimed_effect: Resolve rate +3 to +5 points on full Verified across four LLMs; 62->76 on a 50-problem subset; 45.8% on Pro
signatures.failure_boundary: GPT-5-Nano collapses (44->14), GPT-5-Mini slightly down on the subset; tool count does not correlate with solve rate

signatures.object: The per-step feedback prompt of the agent loop (reflection message appended to every observation) and the initial instruction to create at least an edit tool
signatures.operation: Append 'Reflect on the previous trajectories and decide if there are any tools you can create...' after every command output
signatures.output: A per-step decision point on tool creation (and an extra reasoning nudge)
signatures.conditions: Output shorter than 10k chars (otherwise the warning variant replaces the reflection text)
signatures.persistence: Prompt template (human-authored, fixed across all benchmarks except a path change)
signatures.later_use: Applied at every step of every issue
signatures.claimed_effect: Reflection raises resolve rate 64->76 and tool count 2.92->3.28 on the 50-problem subset
signatures.failure_boundary: Effect confounded with generic extra reflection; no reflection-without-tool-creation control

gap.author_gap: Agents have fixed scaffolds and static action spaces; manual scaffold design is costly; offline self-improving agents (SICA/DGM/HGM) are expensive (~$22k per DGM run) and specialize to benchmark and LLM.
gap.checked_gap: Cost and specialization of offline scaffold evolution is a sourced, concrete bottleneck (DGM cost quoted from original paper, E001; offline hours in Table 2, E008). 'Static action space' as a bottleneck is argued by example (silent sed failures, multi-step grep) rather than measured.
gap.lineage: mini-SWE-agent (bash only) -> SWE-agent (hand-crafted tools, ~7k LOC) -> SICA/DGM/HGM (offline scaffold self-modification on benchmarks) -> Live-SWE-agent (runtime tool synthesis driven by a prompt). Prior tool-creation work for reasoning/embodied tasks is only cited, not compared.
gap.closest_adjacent: DGM/HGM/SICA (same object, offline, benchmark-selected); LATM/CREATOR-style tool-making for non-SWE tasks (named in related work, source text not fixed locally).
gap.residue: Whether runtime-created tools can be kept, validated and reused across issues; whether the gain comes from tool creation or from the added prompt/reflection; behaviour on weaker LLMs.
gap.stakes: Scaffold design cost and the transfer of evolved agents across LLMs/benchmarks.
gap.method_response: Moves evolution to inference time and makes tool creation a per-step decision; avoids offline cost entirely.
gap.remaining_gap: No cross-task retention (E013), no admission/regression gate, no attribution beyond a bundled prompt ablation, weak-LLM failure, leaderboard superiority confounded by differing base LLMs.
gap.unresolved: Nearest neighbours in LLM tool-making literature were not available as fixed local sources; novelty claim 'first live software agent' not independently checked.

rs_pattern.reason: Both seats generative_process_redesign, sub null; re-checked and kept. The conventionally fixed component of an iterative agent loop (its tool/action inventory) becomes a runtime variable; same ruling as SICA (r03b) and Gödel Agent (cal-dev). C15/C23/C24 (3D substrate, diffusion chain, conditioning granularity) do not fit, so sub null. decompose_and_delegate/C25 (LATM/Alita convention) not used: there is no maker/user split or checker-closed admission — the single agent writes and uses its scripts unverified.

matches.tactic_steps_checked: Named the fixed component (static action space) with stated reason (hand-designed scaffolds, E001/Sec 1) and ablated removal of tool creation (E005). Not done: separation of the redesign from co-varying prompt content; strongest baseline on same scaffold on Pro; mechanism/theory.
matches.success_checks: Component named: yes. Ablation collapse: partial (62 vs 76, bundled). Order-of-magnitude or incumbent-matching payoff: partial (best open result at time of writing, authors' claim). No retraining/frozen model: yes.
matches.failure_checks: 'Fixed component is bottleneck' asserted by example not measured: partially present. Strong baseline omitted: partly (same-scaffold control absent on Pro).
matches.sub_card_note: C15/C23/C24 are 3D-representation, diffusion-chain and conditioning-interface tactics; none corresponds to tool-set liberation, so sub_id=null.
matches.reason: Operation (not mere mention): the agent's inventory is made mutable during the loop.

matches.condition_checks: H07-step1 gap-detection decision: partial (reflection fires every step). Step2 grounding: unmet (model knowledge only). Step3 sandbox build/repair: partial (agent runs and edits its scripts). Step4 registration/description: unmet. Step5 reuse on tasks that did not produce the tool + retained-inventory ablation: unmet (tools are discarded, E013). S1 execution admission gate: unmet. F1 buried in larger architecture: not present (isolated prompt-only change).

revision_proposals: Consider a sub-condition for within-episode (non-persistent) tool synthesis: H07 assumes registration and later-task reuse.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: free the fixed component of an iterative procedure. Domain: agent forges tools when a capability gap appears mid-task. Both = make the agent's action inventory mutable at runtime.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_or_differences: Domain card additionally requires admission by execution, registration and cross-task reuse; the paper only has in-episode scripts.

claims.text: Live-SWE-agent raises SWE-bench Verified resolve rate over mini-SWE-agent for four LLMs (Claude 4.5 Sonnet 70.6->75.4, Gemini 3 Pro 74.2->77.4, GPT-5 65.0->68.4, GPT-5-Mini 59.8->63.0).
claims.setting: 500 problems, one sample per issue, 250 steps/$3 caps
claims.selection_vs_test: No selection stage; prompt development data not described
claims.result_denominator: % resolved of 500; failed runs counted as unresolved
claims.counterevidence: single run; baseline prompt differs in more than tool creation
claims.allowed_conclusion: Prompting for runtime tool scripts is associated with +3 to +5 points on Verified for these four LLMs; cause not separated from added reflection prompt.

claims.text: Both tool creation and the per-step reflection matter (62 -> 64 -> 76).
claims.allowed_conclusion: On this subset the full prompt solved 6 more problems than the tool-creation-without-reflection prompt; direction plausible, magnitude uncertain.

claims.text: 45.8% on SWE-Bench Pro, best known, beating SWE-agent 43.6%.
claims.selection_vs_test: Pro is a separate benchmark, prompt unchanged except path
claims.counterevidence: baseline reused, different scaffold; no mini-SWE-agent control on Pro
claims.allowed_conclusion: Live-SWE-agent scores 2.2 points above the reported SWE-agent figure; not attributable to tool creation alone.

claims.text: Beats DGM/HGM/SICA on Verified-60 (65.0 vs 56.7/53.3/50.0) with zero offline cost.
claims.baseline_control: published numbers of offline self-improving agents
claims.counterevidence: baseline numbers reused; per-issue inference cost of baselines not compared; the same GPT-5-Mini on the 50-problem subset shows 58.0 vs 60.0 for the baseline (E018)
claims.allowed_conclusion: On this 60-problem subset Live-SWE-agent's single-run score exceeds the published scores; cost advantage covers offline cost only.

claims.text: The agent 'autonomously and continuously evolves itself on the fly' (central framing).
claims.counterevidence: tools discarded per task (E013); no gate; weak LLMs degrade (E010)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Within-episode synthesis of helper scripts; cross-task retained self-improvement is not shown.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A prompt that asks a strong LLM to write and reuse helper scripts during one issue is associated with +3 to +5 points of single-run resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified across four LLMs, and +6 on a 50-problem multilingual subset, at modest extra cost.
assessment.cannot_say: That tools are retained or improve later tasks; that tool creation (rather than the added reflection prompt) causes the gain; that it beats offline self-evolving agents under matched LLM/budget; ranking claims versus agents run with other LLMs.
unresolved: Prompt development split; contamination of Verified for the tested LLMs; tool-usage statistics.
Whether created tools are actually invoked in resolved instances (no tool-use or credit analysis, opus:O01).
assessment.reproduction_note: All results are author-reported; nothing re-run by us.

G.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Sourced bottleneck for offline self-improvers (~$22k DGM run, 512–1231 offline hours, benchmark/LLM specialisation) with clear SICA/DGM/HGM lineage; the residual (runtime, per-issue tooling, no offline cost) is stated. Not 4: runtime tool-making neighbours (LATM/CREATOR-type) are dismissed in one sentence as 'not SE', and 'static action space is limiting' is argued by example.

M.reason: Opus sides with son55. Mechanism is concrete (script tools + per-step reflection prompt) with plausible reasons (silent sed failures, multi-step searches) and one confirmed prediction (stronger LLMs gain more, weak ones loop). But in this domain's M criterion there is no accept/reject step and no write-back beyond the trajectory, and the key assumption — that tool creation rather than the per-step reflection nudge drives the gain — is untested and partly contradicted by the paper's own tool counts (opus:O01). sol's 3 credited reconstructibility, which is scored under X.

X.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Operation chain, interface (script via bash), caps and exact prompts are fully given (App. D) and the boundaries are explicit (discard after task, weak-LLM looping). Not 4: no admission gate, versioning, rollback or cross-task read.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Official hidden-test resolve rates on full Verified (500), Pro (731) and a Multilingual subset; the verifier is not touched by the agent. Not 4: single sample per issue and benchmark-test weakness is not discussed; cross-LLM leaderboard mixing is a causality issue (A2).

E.causality.reason: Opus sides with son55. Same-scaffold, same-cap comparisons on full Verified across four LLMs (+3.2 to +4.8) support the bundled prompt change. Attribution to tools is not established: the 'w/o tool creation' arm is the base agent, the reflection message bundles extra deliberation with the tool nudge (opus:O02), the 12-point reflection effect comes with nearly equal tool counts (opus:O01), there is no tools-given or reflection-only control, and DGM/HGM/SWE-agent numbers are reused rather than rerun (son55:E009). Single runs are charged to E.statistics (A2), not here.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Nothing is selected on evaluation data, Pro and Multilingual act as out-of-benchmark checks with an unchanged prompt; but the prompt's development data are undescribed, the ablation subset is drawn from Verified, contamination of public benchmarks is not addressed, and cross-task retention is untested (opus:O03).

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked (A2 ladder: sample sizes and negative results reported, no uncertainty on main results). Single runs, no intervals; 50-problem subsets with 6–7-problem gaps; subset vs full-set inconsistency for GPT-5-Mini.

E.cost.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Average $ per issue for both arms under the same 250-step/$3 caps, including tool-creation overhead; offline hours of DGM/HGM contrasted. Not 4: no token/step counts, Pro baseline cost missing, offline baselines not budget-matched.

reason: Complete pinned v3 text incl. Appendices A–D read; in scope (system_method, boundary): agent-written tool scripts are a non-weight action-space component created from execution feedback and reused within one trajectory; not retained across tasks (opus:O03). All eight items resolved.

Applies (card kept). Removing tool creation lowers 76→62, but the arm also removes the reflection prompt and how often the static action space actually binds is not measured.

Verified: same-LLM comparisons exist (4 LLMs), but the headline 'beats all agents' compares Live-SWE+Gemini 3 Pro with systems on other LLMs.
Failure avoided: the change is an isolated prompt on the unmodified mini-SWE-agent loop, so the forging effect is the measured contribution.
Verified: an explicit decision point exists but fires on every step rather than on a detected gap (the noise/latency risk the card names); weak LLMs loop.

S1 asks for an execution-based admission gate. No admission step exists: scripts are used as soon as written and only the agent's own later runs reveal faults. sol's 'partial' credited use and reuse, which is not a gate.

See ratings.M: no accept/reject or write-back beyond the trajectory, and the tools-not-reflection assumption is untested and weakened by Table 4's tool counts (opus:O01). Reconstructibility (sol's basis) is credited under X.

See ratings.E.causality: the bundle is supported by same-scaffold comparisons, but the strongest alternative (per-step reflection without tools) is untested and the paper's own tool counts are consistent with it; external baselines are reused. Single-run noise is A2-charged to E.statistics, so sol's 3 was not lowered for that.
